questions.q: The functional anatomy of the liver was described by:
questions.exp: Functional anatomy of the liver is described by Couinaud. (Book p245)

questions.q: The liver is divided into how many functional segments?
questions.exp: The liver is divided into 8 functional segments. (Book p245)

questions.q: The bare area of the liver is most commonly involved in:
questions.exp: The bare area of the liver is the m/c site involved in amoebic liver abscess. (Book p245)

questions.q: The gallbladder fossa is formed by segments:
questions.exp: GB fossa: segments 4B and 5. (Book p245)

questions.q: Because the gallbladder fossa is formed by segments 4B and 5, gallbladder cancer is resected by:
questions.exp: The page notes the GB fossa segments can be involved in GB cancer and are therefore resected in a radical cholecystectomy. (Book p245)

questions.q: Functional classification of the liver is based on:
opts: The portal vein more than the hepatic vein
The hepatic vein more than the portal vein
questions.exp: Functional classification is based on the portal vein rather than the hepatic vein. (Book p245)

questions.q: How many sectors does the liver have?
questions.exp: There are 4 sectors: right posterior, right anterior, left medial and left lateral. (Book p245)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four sectors of the liver?
questions.exp: The four sectors are right posterior, right anterior, left medial and left lateral. (Book p245)

questions.q: The three major fissures of the liver are related to the:
opts: Hepatic veins — right, left and middle
Portal veins — right, left and main
Sectoral branches of the hepatic artery
questions.exp: Major fissures: 3 fissures related to the right hepatic vein, left hepatic vein and middle hepatic vein. (Book p245)

questions.q: The three minor fissures of the liver are related to all of the following EXCEPT the:
questions.exp: Minor fissures: 3 fissures — right portal vein, left portal vein and the fissure of Ganz. (Book p245)

questions.q: Segment I of the liver is the:
questions.exp: Segment I is the caudate lobe. (Book p245)

questions.q: The caudate lobe lies:
opts: Posteriorly, to the left of the IVC
Anteriorly, to the right of the IVC
Within the left lobe above the falciform ligament
questions.exp: The caudate lobe lies posteriorly, to the left of the IVC. (Book p245)

questions.q: The caudate lobe is called an independent segment because it drains bile into:
opts: Both the left and the right lobes
questions.exp: Segment I drains bile into both left and right lobe ducts — one reason it is called an independent segment. (Book p245)

questions.q: The blood supply of the caudate lobe comes from:
opts: Both the left and the right lobes
questions.exp: Segment I receives blood from both the left and the right lobes. (Book p245)

questions.q: The caudate lobe drains directly into the:
opts: Hepatic vein confluence via the middle hepatic vein
questions.exp: It has direct venous drainage into the IVC. (Book p245)

questions.q: Segment I undergoes compensatory hypertrophy in:
questions.exp: Because it drains directly into the IVC, segment I hypertrophies in Budd-Chiari syndrome. (Book p245)

questions.q: According to the Brisbane classification, a left hepatectomy removes segments:
questions.exp: Left hepatectomy: segments 4A, 4B, 2 and 3. (Book p246)

questions.q: A right hepatectomy removes segments:
questions.exp: Right hepatectomy: segments 5, 6, 7 and 8. (Book p246)

questions.q: A left trisectorectomy removes:
questions.exp: Left trisectorectomy: 4A, 4B, 2, 3 + 5, 8. (Book p246)

questions.q: A right trisectorectomy removes:
questions.exp: Right trisectorectomy: 5, 6, 7, 8 + 4A, 4B. (Book p246)

questions.q: The old name for a left trisectorectomy is:
questions.exp: Left trisectorectomy was formerly called an extended left hepatectomy. (Book p246)

questions.q: The old name for a right trisectorectomy is:
questions.exp: Right trisectorectomy was formerly called an extended right hepatectomy. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
questions.q: The liver has a dual blood supply: portal vein contributes about:
questions.exp: Dual blood supply: portal vein 80% and hepatic artery 20%. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
questions.q: The hepatic artery contributes approximately what fraction of hepatic blood flow?
questions.exp: Portal vein 80% + hepatic artery 20%. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
questions.q: Which hepatic artery is described as larger and supplying the majority of the liver?
questions.exp: Right hepatic artery: larger, supplies the majority of the liver. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
questions.q: In the 'Mickey mouse sign' of the liver pedicle, the portal vein lies:
questions.exp: Mickey mouse sign: portal vein posteriorly, CBD to the right (dextra) and hepatic artery to the left. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
questions.q: In the Mickey mouse sign, the CBD lies to the __________ and the hepatic artery to the __________.
questions.exp: CBD (dextra = right), hepatic artery (left), portal vein (posteriorly). (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: All of the following are listed as normal liver functions EXCEPT:
opts: pH balance and correction of acidosis
questions.exp: The listed functions are: maintaining core body temperature, pH balance and correction of acidosis, synthesis of clotting factors, glucose metabolism, bilirubin formation from Hb degradation, drug and hormone metabolism/excretion and removal of endotoxins and foreign antigens. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: Which liver function is listed as number 3 and, when it fails, produces a bleeding tendency?
questions.exp: Function 3 is synthesis of clotting factors — its failure in liver dysfunction causes bleeding. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: Bilirubin is formed from:
questions.exp: Bilirubin formation from Hb degradation is listed as a normal liver function. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: Failure of the liver to remove endotoxins and foreign antigens is one of the mechanisms behind:
questions.exp: The page links liver dysfunction with encephalopathy. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: Liver function tests listed in this chapter include:
opts: Liver enzymes and clotting factor tests
questions.exp: Liver function tests (LFT): liver enzymes and clotting factor tests. (Book p246)

questions.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
questions.q: The investigation of choice that differentiates HCC from metastasis is:
questions.exp: Triple phase CT is the IOC and is specifically said to differentiate between HCC and metastases. (Book p246)

questions.q: Each clinical/laboratory criterion in the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score is allotted points from:
questions.exp: The scoring columns are 1, 2 and 3 points for each criterion. (Book p247)

questions.q: In the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, severe encephalopathy (grades 3 or 4) scores:
questions.exp: Encephalopathy: none = 1, mild to moderate (grades I or II) = 2, severe (grades 3 or 4) = 3. (Book p247)

questions.q: Diuretic refractory ascites in the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score is graded as:
questions.exp: Ascites: none = 1, mild to moderate/diuretic responsive = 2, severe/diuretic refractory = 3. (Book p247)

questions.q: In the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, a bilirubin of 2-3 mg/dL scores:
questions.exp: Bilirubin (mg/dL): <2 = 1, 2-3 = 2, >3 = 3. (Book p247)

questions.q: An albumin of 2.8-3.5 g/dL scores how many points in the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score?
In the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score the prothrombin time columns are:
questions.exp: Prothrombin time (s): <4 = 1, 4-6 = 2, >6 = 3 (or the INR equivalent: <1.7, 1.7-2.3, >2.3). (Book p247)

questions.q: The INR values used in the Child-Turcotte-Pugh score are:
questions.exp: International normalised ratio (INR): <1.7 = 1, 1.7-2.3 = 2, >2.3 = 3. (Book p247)

questions.q: Child-Turcotte-Pugh class A corresponds to a total score of:
questions.exp: Class A: 5-6 (least severe). (Book p247)

questions.q: Child-Turcotte-Pugh class B corresponds to a total score of:
questions.exp: Class B: 7-9 (moderately severe). (Book p247)

questions.q: Child-Turcotte-Pugh class C corresponds to a total score of:
questions.exp: Class C: 10-15 (most severe). (Book p247)

questions.q: The surgical mortality quoted for Child-Pugh class A is:
questions.exp: Correlates with surgical mortality: class A 10%. (Book p247)

questions.q: The surgical mortality quoted for Child-Pugh class C is:
questions.exp: Class C carries about 70% surgical mortality. (Book p247)

questions.q: A cirrhotic patient with bilirubin 4 mg/dL, albumin 2.5 g/dL, INR 2.6, moderate ascites and grade II encephalopathy falls into Child class:
opts: Cannot be scored without a biopsy
questions.exp: Bilirubin >3 (3), albumin <2.8 (3), INR >2.3 (3), moderate ascites (2) and grade I-II encephalopathy (2) = 13 points, i.e. class C (10-15). (Book p247)

questions.q: The MELD score uses which three parameters?
questions.exp: Parameters involved in MELD: S. bilirubin, INR and creatinine. (Book p247)

questions.q: With a MELD score of 20 or less, mortality rises by:
questions.exp: Score ≤20: mortality ↑ 1% per score. (Book p247)

questions.q: With a MELD score above 20, mortality rises by:
questions.exp: Score >20: mortality ↑ 2% per score after 20. (Book p247)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a parameter of the PELD score?
questions.exp: PELD parameters: albumin, total bilirubin, INR, growth failure and age (<1 year). (Book p247)

questions.q: The age criterion used in the PELD score is:
questions.exp: Age (<1 yr) is one of the five PELD parameters — PELD is the paediatric score. (Book p247)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The organism causing an amoebic liver abscess is:
questions.exp: Amoebic liver abscess is caused by Entamoeba histolytica. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Amoebic liver abscess reaches the liver by which route?
questions.exp: Route of spread for amoebic abscess: the portal vein (which has laminar flow to the right side). (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The laminar portal flow to the right side explains why amoebic abscesses are most common in the:
questions.exp: Because portal flow preferentially streams to the right side, the right lobe (bare area, segment 7) is most often involved. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The most common route of spread for a pyogenic liver abscess is:
opts: Direct spread from a perforated ulcer
questions.exp: Pyogenic abscess: ascending cholangitis. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The commonest organism overall in a pyogenic liver abscess is:
questions.exp: Pyogenic abscess: polymicrobial (40%), m/c overall E. coli. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The commonest organism causing pyogenic liver abscess in Asia is:
questions.exp: m/c in Asia: Klebsiella. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: A child with chronic granulomatous disease and a liver abscess is most likely to grow:
questions.exp: m/c in children with CGD: S. aureus. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Pyogenic liver abscess pus is typically:
questions.exp: Polymicrobial (40%) is quoted for pyogenic liver abscess. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: CGD in the liver abscess table expands to:
questions.exp: CGD: Chronic granulomatous disease. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Amoebic liver abscesses are usually:
questions.exp: Number: usually solitary in amoebic disease; solitary or multiple in pyogenic disease. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The most common laboratory abnormality in amoebic liver abscess is:
questions.exp: Labs in amoebic abscess: ↑ PT/INR (m/c) and serology positive for Entamoeba. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: A raised ALP in a pyogenic liver abscess is attributed to:
questions.exp: Pyogenic abscess labs: ↑ ALP (due to cholangitis), ↑ PT/INR and ↑ S. bilirubin. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The diagnosis of an amoebic liver abscess is supported by:
questions.exp: Serology positive for Entamoeba is listed under the labs for amoebic abscess. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Flask-shaped ulcers in the gut are associated with:
opts: Amoebic colitis only, never with liver abscess
questions.exp: Ulcers in the gut (flask-shaped) appear in the amoebic column. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Compared with an amoebic abscess, a patient with a pyogenic liver abscess is:
questions.exp: Clinical features: amoebic — pain and fever; pyogenic — more sick, ↑ jaundice. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: The pus of an amoebic liver abscess is classically described as:
questions.exp: Amoebic pus is anchovy-sauce pus, in contrast to the neutrophil-rich pus of a pyogenic abscess. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Epidemiologically both amoebic and pyogenic liver abscess are:
questions.exp: Epidemiology: males > females for both; pyogenic abscess is also associated with immunocompromise. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
questions.q: Immunocompromised state is listed as a predisposition for:
questions.exp: Immunocompromised is listed in the pyogenic column. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: The investigation of choice for a liver abscess is:
questions.exp: IOC: CECT abdomen. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: On imaging, a liver abscess appears as:
opts: An abscess cavity with hypoechoic liquefied pus
A multiloculated cystic lesion with daughter cysts
questions.exp: Abscess cavity with hypoechoic liquefied pus. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: Radiological resolution of the abscess cavity after treatment takes:
questions.exp: Radiological resolution of the cavity takes months (post-Rx), so imaging is not used to judge early response. (Book p248)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: The drug used for an amoebic liver abscess in this chapter is:
questions.exp: A. Amoebic liver abscess: metronidazole (double strength: 800 mg TID). (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: Response to metronidazole is judged after:
questions.exp: After 4-5 days the fever and pain should settle. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: The total duration of metronidazole therapy recommended here is:
questions.exp: After the initial 4-5 days and a fall in fever and pain, treatment is continued for 2-3 weeks. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: After completion of the course of metronidazole, the patient should receive:
opts: A luminal amoebicide — diloxanide furoate for 10 days
questions.exp: After completion of the course, a luminal amoebicide (diloxanide furoate × 10 days) is given. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: If an amoebic abscess does not respond to metronidazole, the next step is:
opts: Aspiration of pus under USG/CT guidance
questions.exp: Not responding → aspiration of pus (USG/CT guided). (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an indication for aspirating an amoebic liver abscess?
questions.exp: Other indications listed: abscess cavity >5 cm, pregnant patient, impending rupture and a left lobe abscess (which can rupture into the pericardium). (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: A left lobe amoebic liver abscess is aspirated early because it can rupture into the:
opts: Pleural cavity only on the right
questions.exp: Left lobe liver abscess can rupture into the pericardium. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
questions.q: A pigtail catheter is used for:
opts: Aspiration of pus anywhere in the abdominal cavity under USG/CT guidance
questions.exp: Pigtail catheter: aspiration of pus anywhere in the abdominal cavity under USG/CT guidance. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
questions.q: First-line treatment of a pyogenic liver abscess is:
questions.exp: B. Pyogenic liver abscess: IV antibiotics, broad spectrum. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
questions.q: The threshold for aspiration in a pyogenic liver abscess should be:
opts: Low — aspirate quickly with a pigtail catheter if the patient is not responding
Same as for an amoebic abscess (wait 2-3 weeks)
questions.exp: Low threshold for aspiration: if the patient is not responding, aspirate quickly with a pigtail catheter. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
questions.q: The most common site of rupture of an amoebic liver abscess is the:
questions.exp: Rupture: sub-diaphragmatic space (m/c), then pleural, peritoneal and pericardial cavities. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a rupture site of an amoebic liver abscess?
questions.exp: The listed sites are sub-diaphragmatic (m/c), pleural, peritoneal and pericardial. (Book p249)

questions.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
questions.q: Secondary infection is listed as a complication of:
questions.exp: Complications of amoebic liver abscess: rupture (into four sites) and secondary infection. (Book p249)

questions.q: The organism causing hydatid disease of the liver is:
questions.exp: Organism: Echinococcus granulosus (E. multilocularis causes malignant hydatid). (Book p250)

questions.q: Echinococcus multilocularis is described as causing:
questions.exp: E. multilocularis is labelled as malignant hydatid. (Book p250)

questions.q: The definitive host of Echinococcus granulosus is the:
questions.exp: Definitive host: dog. (Book p250)

questions.q: The intermediate host of Echinococcus granulosus is the:
questions.exp: Intermediate host: sheep. (Book p250)

questions.q: Man is the:
questions.exp: Accidental intermediate host: man (male = female). (Book p250)

questions.q: The gross appearance of a hydatid cyst is:
questions.exp: Gross anatomy: pearly white cyst. (Book p250)

questions.q: The most common organ affected by hydatid disease is the:
questions.exp: Organs affected: liver (m/c), lungs (2nd m/c), kidneys and spleen. (Book p250)

questions.q: The second most common organ affected by hydatid disease is the:
questions.exp: Lungs are the second most common site after the liver. (Book p250)

questions.q: Most patients with hydatid disease of the liver are:
questions.exp: Clinical features: asymptomatic (majority), right hypochondrial pain, hepatomegaly. (Book p250)

questions.q: The outermost layer of a hydatid cyst, formed by the host, is the:
questions.exp: Pericyst is the host reaction — the page notes it is not a true layer of the parasite. (Book p250)

questions.q: From outside inwards the layers of a hydatid cyst are:
questions.exp: The diagram labels pericyst (host reaction), ectocyst, endocyst and hydatid fluid from outside in. (Book p250)

questions.q: The classification of hydatid cysts used here is based on:
questions.exp: Classification: based on CECT. (Book p250)

questions.q: The two classification systems quoted are:
questions.exp: The table headings are WHO IWG 2001 and Gharbi 1981. (Book p250)

questions.q: A CE1 (Gharbi type I) cyst is described as:
opts: A unilocular cyst with a double line sign
questions.exp: CE1 / Type I: unilocular cyst with a double line sign, and it is an active cyst. (Book p250)

questions.q: A CE2 (Gharbi type II) cyst is:
opts: A cyst with a water-lily sign
questions.exp: CE2 / Type II: multiseptate, honeycomb cyst — active. (Book p250)

questions.q: The water-lily sign is seen in which cyst type?
questions.exp: Water-lily sign: CE3a. (Book p250)

questions.q: A CE3a cyst shows:
opts: Daughter cysts in a solid matrix
questions.exp: CE3a / Type III: cyst with detached membranes — the water-lily sign; a transitional stage. (Book p251)

questions.q: A CE3b cyst shows:
opts: A daughter cyst within a solid matrix
questions.exp: CE3b / Type III: cyst with daughter cyst in a solid matrix — transitional. (Book p251)

questions.q: A CE4 cyst is:
opts: A heterogenous cyst with no daughter cysts and is inactive
A cyst with a water-lily sign
questions.exp: CE4 / Type IV: heterogenous cyst with no daughter cysts — inactive. (Book p251)

questions.q: A CE5 cyst is:
questions.exp: CE5 / Type V: solid/calcified cyst — inactive. (Book p251)

questions.q: Which cyst stages are described as being on the verge of dying and needing no treatment?
questions.exp: Note: CE4 and CE5 do not require treatment — they are on the verge of dying. (Book p251)

questions.q: Which of the following hydatid cyst stages is ACTIVE?
questions.exp: CE1 and CE2 are active; CE3a and CE3b are transitional; CE4 and CE5 are inactive. (Book p251)

questions.q: Which hydatid stage is transitional?
questions.exp: CE3a and CE3b are the transitional stages. (Book p251)

questions.q: The first-line drug before any intervention for hydatid disease is:
questions.exp: 1st line: albendazole, given for a minimum of 7-10 days before intervention. (Book p251)

questions.q: Albendazole should be started at least how long before an intervention?
questions.exp: Albendazole: minimum 7-10 days before intervention. (Book p251)

questions.q: PAIR expands to:
questions.exp: PAIR: percutaneous aspiration, injection and re-aspiration. (Book p251)

questions.q: PAIR is described as the:
opts: Treatment of choice for CE5 cysts
questions.exp: PAIR is stated to be the 1st line intervention. (Book p251)

questions.q: The first step of PAIR is:
opts: Percutaneous aspiration of fluid under image guidance
questions.exp: Step 1: percutaneous aspiration of fluid under image guidance. (Book p251)

questions.q: The most commonly used scolicidal agent is:
questions.exp: Hypertonic saline is listed as the m/c scolicidal agent. (Book p251)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a scolicidal agent?
questions.exp: Scolicidal agents listed: hypertonic saline (m/c), ethanol, absolute alcohol, cetrimide solution and mebendazole solution. (Book p251)

questions.q: Formalin is not used as a scolicidal agent because it causes:
questions.exp: Note: formalin is not a scolicidal agent because it causes chemical cholangitis. (Book p251)

questions.q: The danger of leaking hydatid fluid into the circulation is:
questions.exp: Hydatid fluid can cause anaphylaxis if it leaks into the circulation. (Book p251)

questions.q: The final step of the PAIR procedure is:
questions.exp: Step 3 of PAIR is re-aspiration. (Book p251)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: All of the following are contraindications to PAIR EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Contraindications: dead/calcified cyst, deep seated cyst, impending rupture, multi-septate cyst and extrahepatic cysts. A unilocular CE1 cyst is the ideal indication. (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: A multi-septate hydatid cyst:
opts: Is a contraindication to PAIR, although it can be tried if there are multiple uniloculated cysts
Is the best indication for PAIR
questions.exp: Multi-septate cyst is listed as a contraindication, with the note that PAIR can be tried if there are multiple uniloculated cysts. (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: If bile is aspirated during PAIR, the correct action is to:
questions.exp: Cysto-biliary communication: if bile is aspirated, abandon PAIR because the scolicidal agent would cause chemical cholangitis. (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: Surgery for hydatid disease is indicated when:
opts: The patient is asymptomatic with a CE4 cyst
questions.exp: Surgery is done when PAIR is contraindicated. (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: Which of the following is a surgical option for hydatid disease?
questions.exp: Surgical options listed: cystopericystectomy and liver resection (if multiple cysts in one segment). (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: Multiple hydatid cysts confined to one segment are best treated by:
questions.exp: Liver resection is the option when there are multiple cysts in one segment. (Book p252)

questions.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
questions.q: Capitonnage means:
opts: Spiral closure of the cyst cavity after removal of the cyst
Injection of a scolicidal agent into the cavity
questions.exp: Capitonnage: spiral closure of the cyst cavity after removal of the cyst. (Book p252)

units.title: Functional Anatomy of the Liver
units.sec: Functional Anatomy of the Liver · p245
units.guide: Couinaud gave the surgeon a map, not a description: eight functional segments drawn around the portal vein, with three hepatic veins in the major fissures and the portal branches in the minor ones. Learn the map, because every resection in this chapter is named from it.

units.title: Segment I: The Caudate Lobe
units.sec: Segment I: The Caudate Lobe · p245
units.guide: Segment I is the liver's free agent. The caudate lobe sits behind, to the left of the IVC, takes blood and drains bile from both sides and empties straight into the IVC — which is exactly why it hypertrophies when the hepatic veins thrombose in Budd-Chiari.

units.title: Brisbane Classification of Liver Resection
units.sec: Brisbane Classification of Liver Resection · p246
units.guide: Brisbane turned anatomy into a vocabulary: left hepatectomy is 2, 3, 4A, 4B; right is 5, 6, 7, 8; and each trisectorectomy adds the opposite central segments. Say the numbers and the operation names follow.

units.title: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle
units.sec: Blood Supply and the Liver Pedicle · p246
units.guide: Two vessels feed the liver, the portal vein giving 80% and the hepatic artery 20%, and the right hepatic artery is the larger of the two arteries. At the hilum they line up with the bile duct as the Mickey mouse sign — the landmark that keeps a resection out of trouble.

units.title: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment
units.sec: Functions of the Liver and Their Assessment · p246
units.guide: The liver does far more than make bile: temperature, acid-base, clotting factors, glucose, bilirubin, drug and hormone clearance and endotoxin removal. When it fails, encephalopathy follows; when you need a picture, triple phase CT separates HCC from metastases.

units.title: Child-Turcotte-Pugh Score
units.guide: Child-Turcotte-Pugh is five everyday variables scored 1 to 3 — encephalopathy, ascites, bilirubin, albumin and PT/INR. Add them: A is 5-6, B is 7-9, C is 10-15, and surgical mortality climbs 10%, 30%, 70% across those classes.

units.title: MELD and PELD Scores
units.guide: MELD replaced guesswork with three numbers — bilirubin, INR and creatinine — and each point above a score of 20 costs roughly 2% mortality. PELD is the same idea for infants, adding albumin, growth failure and age under one year.

units.title: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features
units.sec: Liver Abscess: Types and Clinical Features · p248
units.guide: Every column of the abscess table earns its place: amoebic means Entamoeba, portal spread, right lobe, solitary, anchovy-sauce pus and a modestly ill patient; pyogenic means biliary spread, polymicrobial or Klebsiella in Asia, neutrophil-rich pus and a sicker, jaundiced patient.

units.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess
units.sec: Diagnosis and Treatment of Amoebic Liver Abscess · p248
units.guide: Metronidazole at double strength for 4-5 days tells you whether the abscess will settle; complete 2-3 weeks and then clear the gut lumen with diloxanide furoate. Aspirate when the cavity is over 5 cm, when the patient is pregnant, when rupture threatens or when the abscess sits in the left lobe over the pericardium.

units.title: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess
units.sec: Pyogenic Liver Abscess and Complications of Amoebic Abscess · p249
units.guide: Pyogenic abscesses are different creatures: broad-spectrum IV antibiotics first, and a low threshold to drain with a pigtail if the patient is not improving. Know the four directions an amoebic abscess can rupture, with the sub-diaphragmatic space leading the list.

units.title: Hydatid Disease: Epidemiology and Pathology
units.sec: Hydatid Disease: Epidemiology and Pathology · p250
units.guide: Hydatid disease is a dog-sheep cycle that man stumbles into, and the liver is the organ it favours. The cyst is pearly white, the host wraps it in a pericyst, and most patients feel nothing at all until it presses or complicates.

units.title: Classification of Hydatid Cysts
units.guide: The CECT classification turns a cyst into a stage and a stage into a decision: CE1 and CE2 are active, CE3 with its water-lily sign and daughter cysts is transitional, and CE4/CE5 are dying or dead — the last two need no treatment at all.

units.title: PAIR: Management of Hydatid Cyst
units.sec: PAIR: Management of Hydatid Cyst · p251
units.guide: PAIR — aspirate, inject, re-aspirate — is the first-line intervention after albendazole cover. Hypertonic saline is the commonest scolicide, formalin is forbidden because it causes chemical cholangitis, and leaking hydatid fluid can kill by anaphylaxis.

units.title: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease
units.sec: Contraindications to PAIR and Surgery for Hydatid Disease · p252
units.guide: Know when NOT to puncture: dead, deep, multi-septate, extrahepatic or about to rupture — and if bile comes back, stop, because a scolicide in the biliary tree causes chemical cholangitis. Those cysts go to theatre for cystopericystectomy, resection or capitonnage.
